links.outcome: AF screening effect (incident AF diagnosis rate difference) across AI risk deciles
links.effect: Screening effect seen only in top CH-AI decile: 10.07 vs 7.76/100 person-years, difference 2.32 (95% CI 0.01-4.63), number-needed-to-screen 43 per year; trade-off with reduced population coverage.
links.quote: An AF screening effect was observed in the top decile of CH-AI (AF diagnosis rate in screening 10.07/100 person-years [95% 8.28-11.87] vs 7.76 [95% 6.30-9.21] in control, P < 0.05), corresponding to a difference in AF diagnosis rate of 2.32/100 person-years (95% CI: 0.01-4.63) and number-needed-to-screen of 43 per year.

links.outcome: AF diagnosis rate and number-needed-to-screen in the highest predicted-risk decile
links.effect: In the top CH-AI decile, screening increased AF diagnoses by 2.32/100 person-years (95% CI: 0.01-4.63); number-needed-to-screen was 43 per year.
links.quote: An AF screening effect was observed in the top decile of CH-AI (AF diagnosis rate in screening 10.07/100 person-years [95% 8.28-11.87] vs 7.76 [95% 6.30-9.21] in control, P < 0.05), corresponding to a difference in AF diagnosis rate of 2.32/100 person-years (95% CI: 0.01-4.63) and number-needed-to-screen of 43 per year.
